items: Guests come back when they trust the experience will be the same every visit, so raising your floor matters more than chasing the occasional exceptional night.
Write down what good service looks like, from the greeting to how quickly a table is acknowledged and how to handle mistakes, so your team can train and be measured against it.
Your team treats guests the way leadership treats them, so hire for attitude, communicate clearly and use a short pre-shift briefing to set the tone.
Let staff resolve complaints on the spot, and read reviews and ratings for repeated patterns so you can fix the causes behind them.
